q8.answer: The attempt is stored in Redis under oidc:attempt:{sha256(state)}. It holds the state, nonce, code_verifier, intent, next or origin, user_id (link only) and a flow hash, with a 10-minute TTL. The callback deletes it with GETDEL before any other check, so it is single-use whatever the outcome, and Redis also removes it when the TTL expires. The oidc_flow cookie (Max-Age 10 minutes) carries the random value that the attempt's flow hash is checked against.

q9.answer: The half-finished link (user_id, sub, next) is held in a Redis confirm record under oidc:confirm:{sha256(flow)} with a TTL of 10 minutes from the callback, and retries do not extend it. The browser refers to it only through the oidc_flow cookie, a random 32-byte HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax value whose hash is the record key. The record is deleted on success, on lock, on refusal, or when its TTL expires, and a POST without the cookie gets the same error as an expired record.

q10.answer: The permanent link is the PostgreSQL table google_identities, with sub as TEXT PRIMARY KEY and user_id as BIGINT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, plus linked_at. The primary key enforces one user per Google account, and the UNIQUE constraint on user_id enforces one Google account per user. A duplicate insert raises a unique violation, which the flows treat as a refusal, or in the new-user case as a rollback and a fresh lookup.

q11.answer: The user is sent back to the page they started from (login or Account Settings) with a neutral message, and nothing in the database changes. The exchange is not retried, because the authorization code is single-use, so the user must start a new attempt. A failed ID token check gets the same neutral result, and the failure reason is logged without the code, tokens or nonce.

q12.answer: The attempt record, keyed by the state hash, stores intent as either login or link, and the entry point sets it when the attempt starts. A link attempt also stores the signed-in user_id, while a login attempt stores none. For a link, the callback checks that the browser is still signed in as that user_id and otherwise shows a sign-in-again error with nothing changed, then links the sub to that user.
